payload.stem: The graph of a decreasing positive function $f$ on $[1,8]$ is shown and consists of line segments, and $b_n=f(n)$. The alternating series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{n+1}b_n$ is approximated by its partial sum $S_5$ of the first $5$ terms. Using the alternating series error bound, what is the least upper bound for $|S-S_5|$ that the graph supports, if $b_n$ continues to decrease to $0$ beyond $n=8$?

stimulus.description: Graph of f, consisting of line segments connecting the plotted vertices.

options.why: Uses the last term included in the partial sum, b_5, as the bound.
Reports the partial sum S_5 itself.
Uses the difference b_5 - b_6 of consecutive terms.
The error is at most the first omitted term b_6 = f(6), read from the graph.

key_scoring.notes: The stem asks for the 'least upper bound for |S-S_5| that the graph supports'. The error bound b_6 is a guaranteed bound, not the least upper bound of the actual error. The phrase is mathematically inaccurate and ambiguous, so the key 5 is not strictly defensible as worded.
